issues.description: revoke_error exposed on lease lookup without redaction, sanitization, or auth-level gating despite author flagging it as a security concern
issues.detail: The PR author explicitly asks whether returning RevokeErr is safe, then ships it unresolved. Backend error strings routinely leak paths, endpoints, and credential fragments. Either redact, require sudo/root capability, or document an explicit redaction invariant tied to where revocation errors are constructed before merge.

issues.description: Renaming FetchLeaseTimes to FetchLeaseInfo is cosmetic churn on an exported API and weakens the name's precision
issues.detail: FetchLeaseTimes is an exported method called by out-of-tree consumers; the rename to the vaguer 'Info' breaks them for no functional gain and discards the constraint the old name encoded. Either revert, keep a thin alias, or rename to something precise (e.g., exportableLeaseView) and update the docstring to enumerate the export-safe field set.

issues.description: Test coverage for namespace_path and revoke_error is absent; only path is asserted
issues.detail: TestSystemBackend_leases checks path but exercises neither of the two new conditional fields that carry security-relevant content. Add cases for a lease in a child namespace asserting namespace_path, plus nil/empty/populated RevokeErr cases to pin the contract and redaction behavior.

issues.description: OpenAPI marks path as Required but namespace_path and revoke_error are optional; verify path is always non-empty
issues.detail: Required:true is a contract guarantee. Confirm every leaseEntry reaching handleLeaseLookup has a non-empty Path (including irrevocable leases loaded from disk); otherwise drop Required or schema-generated clients will trust a guarantee the code does not keep.

issues.description: metrics.MeasureSince label still reads 'fetch-lease-times' after the function rename
issues.detail: The telemetry key was not updated with the rename, creating a silent mismatch between code and metric that will confuse ops. Either keep the old name with a comment explaining the deliberate stability choice, or rename the metric explicitly as a known telemetry break.

issues.description: leaseInfoForExport returns *leaseEntry, complecting the redacted export view with the authoritative record
issues.detail: Reusing the same struct for both the in-memory entry and the redacted projection means callers cannot tell from the type which fields are guaranteed present versus absent because redacted. A distinct LeaseView struct with exactly the exported fields would prevent future fields from silently leaking through the same path.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, well-shaped patch that widens the lease-lookup projection with three new fields, but the central question — whether revoke_error is safe to surface on a non-privileged endpoint — was raised by the author and shipped unresolved. All three reviewers want explicit redaction, gating, or a documented invariant before merge. The FetchLeaseTimes-to-FetchLeaseInfo rename draws unanimous criticism as churn on an exported API that also leaves a stale metrics label. Test coverage exercises only path; the two security-relevant new fields are untested. Ship-able after gating/redacting revoke_error, resolving the rename, fixing the metric label, and adding tests for namespace_path and revoke_error.
